4.3.done: Core set 26 of 27: weight_missing_fraction dropped (duplicate, kept volume_missing_fraction). Team collinearity drops: 0 (none flagged in s03). Encoded design matrix: linear: 140 encoded columns, duplicates dropped [missingindicator_total_weight_g; missingindicator_product_photos_qty], 138 columns, rank 138, condition number 1.55e+03; tree: 143 encoded columns, duplicates dropped [missingindicator_total_weight_g; missingindicator_product_photos_qty], 141 columns, rank 139, condition number 7.99e+16.
4.3.reasoning: Rank and condition number are measured once on pre-cutoff rows; the preprocessing fitted for this measurement is not saved. Fields that are always missing together give identical missing indicators, so the 4.3 duplicate rule is applied to the encoded columns inside each training fold (factory step 'dedupe'); the linear/logistic matrix is then full rank. The tree recipe keeps every one-hot level, so its matrix is rank-deficient by design, which does not affect trees.
4.3.label: observation

4.4.reasoning: Declared exception (G-19): the ranking is computed once on pre-cutoff orders, so CV scores of the chosen set are optimistic; the report says so.
4.4.label: observation

4.6.done: feature_dictionary.csv: 33 rows (every pool feature and the derived missing indicators): formula, grain, checkout availability, missingness, transform, imputation, kept and reason, hypothesised signal and claim type; 9 rows cite a source checked in Experiment 5 (9 of 25 kept).
4.6.reasoning: Sources were re-checked in this experiment (round 3, Henry's comment): Deshpande & Pendem (2023) and Leite et al. (2024) support, at abstract level, that longer or late delivery lowers customer ratings, so the classification delivery proxies are literature-supported hypotheses. Cui et al. (2024) studies the promised delivery speed and does not support a location or distance feature, so it is not cited. Every other signal is an unmeasured mechanism, tested only by the models.
4.6.label: literature-supported hypothesis
